A1.evidence: The R scripts can be retrieved by HTTPS DOI resolution (Zenodo, http_status 200) and from GitHub https://github.com/ercrema/diffusionCurve (http_status 200).

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS is open and free. Pack: access_right 'open'.

A1_2.evidence: Fully open, no authentication required. Under the v2.1 open case this satisfies A1.2.

A2.evidence: The Zenodo deposit carries the Row 2 persistence entitlement (tombstone page, metadata always publicly accessible). The GitHub copy has no persistence entitlement (pack persistence_entitlement: false), but the archived Zenodo snapshot is the persistent principal artefact.

F1.evidence: 'All data and R scripts are ... permanently archived on https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942' (p. 7). Pack: DataCite DOI, resource_type 'Software'.

F2.evidence: Structured DataCite/Zenodo metadata record exists (metadata_record: true; publisher, year, resource type 'Software', licence).

F4.evidence: Pack: DataCite state 'findable', so the record is indexed in DataCite and Zenodo.

I1.evidence: Code is in R, an open, formal, widely shared language: 'implemented using the NIMBLE ... probabilistic programming language in R (R Core Team, 2020) and the nimbleCarbon R package' (pp. 5-6).

I2.evidence: No vocabulary or ontology standard for the software metadata is evidenced in the paper or the pack.

I3.evidence: Dependencies are cited, some with PIDs: 'NIMBLE: MCMC, Particle Filtering, and Programmable Hierarchical Modeling. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1211190'; 'nimbleCarbon ... 0.2.0'; R Core Team 2020 (references, p. 10).

R1.evidence: The analysis is richly described: model equations [5]-[12], priors, MCMC settings ('four chains, each with 1 million iterations (half discarded as burn-in) and with thinning set to 50'), ICAR settings, Gelman-Rubin diagnostics (p. 6). The acknowledgements note Ben Marwick 'reviewing the computational code and providing suggestions to improve its reproducibility' (p. 9).

R1_1.evidence: Zenodo records licence cc-by-4.0 for the archived software (pack DataCite and Zenodo). The GitHub record lists no licence (licences: []); that is silence, not a conflicting assertion, and the paper is silent. The licence is identified at the persistent deposit.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance and pipeline are documented: software and versions (R, NIMBLE, nimbleCarbon 0.2.0), the IntCal20 calibration curve ('We used the IntCal20 curve for all models', p. 7), parameters, iterations, burn-in, thinning, and posterior predictive check procedure (pp. 5-7). The CRediT statement attributes software to E.R. Crema.

R1_3.evidence: No evidence in the paper or pack of package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or formal community review (CRAN/JOSS/rOpenSci). The informal pre-publication code review by Ben Marwick is not a community review venue.

A1.evidence: Coverage is complete: 'All data and R scripts are available ... permanently archived on https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942' (p. 7). The compiled case-study datasets and simulated data resolve over HTTPS through the DOI.

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS DOI resolution and open download. Pack: Zenodo access_right 'open', http_status 200.

A1_2.evidence: Fully open resource needing no authentication (pack access_right 'open'). Under instrument v2.1 the open case satisfies A1.2. The radiocarbon dates involve no ethical restrictions.

A2.evidence: Zenodo is the host. Platform table Row 2 entitles a tombstone page on withdrawal with metadata always publicly accessible. The pack confirms the deposit is on Zenodo.

F1.evidence: Data deposited with own DOI: 'permanently archived on https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942' (p. 7). Pack: DataCite DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10782942, state 'findable'.

F2.evidence: Pack shows a structured DataCite/Zenodo metadata record (metadata_record: true; publisher Zenodo; publication_year 2024; resource_type; licence). Platform table rows 1-2 entitle a DataCite metadata record.

F3.evidence: Pack: identifier_in_metadata: true for the DataCite and Zenodo records (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10782942; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10816946).

F4.evidence: Pack: DataCite state 'findable', so the record is indexed in DataCite and Zenodo.

I1.evidence: Neither the paper nor the pack states the data file formats (CSV or otherwise), and no platform-table row covers format. With the ladder exhausted, the unscoreable default gives 0.

I2.evidence: No controlled vocabularies or ontologies (e.g. PeriodO, Pleiades, AAT) are mentioned for the data in the paper or the pack.

I3.evidence: Upstream data sources are cited by bibliographic reference only (Kudo et al. 2023; Crema et al. 2022; Bevan et al. 2017; Bloxam 2020; Healy 2012; Wilkin 2013; Willis et al. 2016). R1.evidence: The paper describes the datasets with many attributes: '1479 14C dates on seed remains from Japan (n = 551, from 215 sites ...) and Britain (n = 928, from 314 sites ...)', taxa used as proxies, filtering windows and probability thresholds, and cremation/inhumation counts (n = 1417 / 1119) (sections 4.1.1-4.1.3, p. 5).

R1_1.evidence: Licence recorded at the hosting service is cc-by-4.0 (pack DataCite and Zenodo records). The paper is silent on the deposit licence and no conflict is flagged, so the service licence is scored per the R1.1 rule.

R1_2.evidence: Sources and processing are documented: 'Japanese dates were collated from the radiocarbon database of Japan (Kudo et al., 2023) and the rice radiocarbon database used in (Crema et al., 2022)'; 'Radiocarbon dates from Britain were obtained from Bevan et al. (2017)'; burial dates come from named sources; filtering criteria (cumulative calibrated probability >=0.5 or >=0.99 in stated windows); simulation parameters (p. 5).
